conflicts.parties: Russia; Ukraine (with Western support)
conflicts.t: Russia’s full-scale invasion of February 2022 continues along a front in the east and south, with independent assessments cited by Al Jazeera on 13 November 2026 putting Russia’s net gain this year at 117 sq km. Ukraine, Russia and the United States held their first talks since February in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November; Russia’s delegation said it would be satisfied only by a peace on its terms, and an exchange of at least 1,000 prisoners a side was agreed. Ukraine says Russia fired 3,519 drones in ten days and 36 ballistic missiles at energy sites on 7 November.
conflicts.fig: UCDP: at least 94,700 killed in 2025, about 62% of all battle deaths worldwide; the Wikipedia list counts 80,245 deaths in 2025 and 42,286 so far in 2026

conflicts.parties: Israel; Hamas and allied factions
conflicts.t: A ceasefire signed by Israel and Hamas in October 2025 holds in name while Israel keeps the part of Gaza behind the ‘Yellow Line’. On 18 November 2026 Israeli tanks pushed into central Gaza east of Nuseirat and north of Bureij in the first broad ground operation since the truce; hospital officials said three Palestinians were killed, Hamas called it a flagrant violation, and Gaza’s health ministry counted seven dead in the previous 24 hours.
conflicts.fig: 74,618 Palestinians reported killed and 175,920 injured since 7 October 2023 (Gaza Ministry of Health, in OCHA’s snapshot of 4 November 2026); more than 1,200 Israelis killed; 597 aid workers killed

conflicts.n: Iran against the United States and Israel
conflicts.parties: Iran; United States; Israel
conflicts.t: The United States and Israel opened a war on Iran on 28 February 2026 with about 900 strikes in under twelve hours; Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in the opening strikes and Mojtaba Khamenei was named his successor on 9 March. Pakistan brokered a two-week truce on 8 April, the US blockaded Iranian ports, and a preliminary agreement to end the war was announced on 14 June after 108 days. On 12 November 2026 Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf called the position ‘no war and no peace’: the blockade and Iranian control of passage through the Strait of Hormuz remain, with Qatar mediating.
conflicts.fig: UCDP counted eight interstate conflicts in 2025, the most since 1946, Iran–Israel among them; the Wikipedia list counts 7,045 deaths in Iran in 2026

conflicts.parties: Israel; Hezbollah; Lebanon
conflicts.t: Hezbollah fired rockets at Israel on 2 March 2026 after the killing of Iran’s supreme leader, and Israel answered with air raids and a ground invasion that left it holding a strip about 10 km deep. A US-brokered framework agreement signed in Washington on 26 June 2026 ties Israeli withdrawal to Hezbollah’s verified disarmament; by 29 July only one pilot zone, Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh, had passed to the Lebanese army, Israeli strikes continue, and Hezbollah rejects the deal.
conflicts.fig: more than 4,200 killed in Lebanon since 2 March 2026 (Lebanese Health Ministry, cited by Al Jazeera on 28 June)

conflicts.parties: Houthis (Ansar Allah); Yemeni government and Southern forces; Saudi-led coalition
conflicts.t: The Houthis, who took Sanaa in 2014, resumed a ground offensive in August 2026, besieged Taiz from early October and on 15 November drove government-aligned forces from the Bab al-Mandeb area; by 16 November they were reported 60–100 km from Aden, the government’s interim capital. The Saudi-led coalition has resumed air strikes and reports intercepting Houthi drones over Riyadh and Mecca; Saudi Arabia named a new Joint Forces commander on 16 November.
conflicts.fig: OCHA: more than 340,000 people displaced since fighting began in August 2026, two-thirds from Taiz (cited by FDD’s Long War Journal, 16 November)

conflicts.parties: Syrian transitional government; Druze Sweida National Guard; Israel; remnants of ISIL
conflicts.t: Ahmad al-Shara’s government has run Damascus since Assad fell in December 2024, and a campaign in January 2026 brought the Kurdish-led SDF under its control after the US ended support. Sweida is the open front: an Israeli-backed Druze ‘National Guard’ holds the hills around the city, and The National reported on 22 October 2026 that Damascus had sent about 3,000 troops to its western approaches while Israel airlifts equipment into the province and keeps positions in Quneitra and Deraa.
conflicts.fig: about 1,700 killed, mostly Druze, in the July 2025 Sweida fighting (The National); the Wikipedia list counts 8,837 deaths in 2025 and 1,575 in 2026

conflicts.parties: Sudanese Armed Forces; Rapid Support Forces and allies
conflicts.t: The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces began in April 2023; the RSF took El Fasher in October 2025 after a long siege and holds all five Darfur states. The army has turned the Kordofan front: on 13 November 2026 it took al-Khuwai in West Kordofan, having broken the siege of El Obeid, while the RSF still holds al-Nuhud and parts of South Kordofan with the SPLM-N.
conflicts.fig: about 150,000 killed and more than 14 million displaced (Al Jazeera, 14 November 2026); UCDP recorded about 76,500 deaths from one-sided violence in 2025, mainly at El Fasher

conflicts.t: The civil war that followed the 2021 coup is in its sixth year. The military held phased elections in December 2025 and January 2026, coup leader Min Aung Hlaing was voted in as president, and on 6 November 2026 the election commission announced by-elections for 4 April 2027 in 39 constituencies, a third of them in areas of Sagaing, Mandalay and Chin where voting had been cancelled for security reasons.

conflicts.parties: DR Congo and allied Wazalendo militias; AFC/M23, renamed FRN, backed by Rwanda
conflicts.t: M23 took Goma and Bukavu in early 2025. A Doha framework of November 2025 and a roadmap agreed in Switzerland in August 2026 have not stopped the fighting: the rebel front, which Critical Threats reports was renamed FRN under Joseph Kabila on 12 October 2026, launched an offensive from Kahuzi-Biega on 6 November and took Bulambika and Bunyakiri on the RN3 by 9 November as government forces fell back toward Irangi.

conflicts.parties: Somali government and AUSSOM; al-Shabaab; ISIL in Puntland
conflicts.t: Al-Shabaab claimed on 26 October 2026 to have killed hundreds of Somali soldiers in an ambush near Leego, a toll not independently verified. Uganda, with about 6,500 troops in the country, said on 2 November it will withdraw by the end of 2027, and US forces left Baledogle airfield in late October while continuing air strikes, the latest on 5 November in Lower Shabelle (FDD’s Long War Journal, 10 November).

conflicts.parties: Ethiopian federal forces and the Tigray Peace Force; TPLF; Fano; Eritrea
conflicts.t: War returned to Tigray in late September 2026: federal forces took Mekelle in early October as the TPLF withdrew, Ethiopia and Eritrea severed ties on 2 October, and Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of leading a rebel offensive, which Asmara denies. By 15 November Eritrean forces had reportedly retaken Badme, Fano fighters clashed with the army southeast of Bahir Dar on 16 November, and a UN delegation began a visit to Mekelle on 17 November (Critical Threats).

conflicts.n: Mali: JNIM and the Azawad front
conflicts.parties: Malian junta and Russia’s Africa Corps; JNIM; Azawad Liberation Front (FLA)
conflicts.t: JNIM’s fuel blockade of Bamako began on 3 September 2025. On 25 April 2026 JNIM and the Tuareg FLA attacked military sites across Mali including the capital, killed Defence Minister Sadio Camara at Kati and took Kidal with about 130 soldiers captured; Russia said its Africa Corps helped thwart a coup, and Assimi Goïta took the defence portfolio himself on 4 May. JNIM declared a full blockade of Bamako on 28 April.

conflicts.parties: Burkinabè junta and VDP militias; JNIM; Islamic State Sahel
conflicts.t: JNIM has fought in Burkina Faso since 2016 and in February 2026 made the country the focus of a coordinated offensive across the central Sahel and into Benin. Human Rights Watch documented the execution of at least 34 civilians at Titao on 14 February and four at Manni on 22 February, and ACLED counted more than 30 JNIM attacks that month with over 120 soldiers, forest guards and militiamen killed. The junta of Ibrahim Traoré has ruled since 2022.

conflicts.t: Niger’s junta, in power since the 2023 coup, fights Islamic State’s Sahel affiliate in the west and JNIM in the south-east. Attackers struck the air base at Niamey’s Diori Hamani airport after midnight on 29 January 2026; ISIL claimed it, the government said 20 attackers were killed, and General Tiani thanked the Russian troops at the base and accused France, Benin and Ivory Coast of sponsoring the raid, without evidence. Attacks in Tillabéri in September 2025 killed more than 120 people.

conflicts.t: The UN says up to 90% of Port-au-Prince is under gang control. The UN-backed Gang Suppression Force began arriving in April 2026 with a mandate to March 2027, and El Salvador sent up to 2,000 troops after four of its technicians were kidnapped on 18 October. On 19 November 2026 Haiti’s army and police, with a task force including Erik Prince’s Vectus Global, fought to clear Martissant on Route 2; police said 34 suspected gang members were killed.

The Sinaloa cartel’s factions, orphaned by the detention of ‘El Chapo’ and ‘El Mayo’ in the US, fight an internal war that has killed thousands; on 11 November 2026 Mexico announced 15 arrests, 14 of them in Chiapas.

conflicts.t: Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban fought openly from late February 2026 after Pakistani air raids and an Afghan cross-border attack; a March ceasefire collapsed and Kabul struck targets in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on 18 June. The UN counted at least 372 Afghan civilians killed in the first three months of 2026. Clashes continued at Angoor Adda and Torkham on 1 November, and on 11 November the TTP ambushed police in Kohat, killing ten (FDD’s Long War Journal, 12 November).

conflicts.t: India struck nine sites in Pakistan on 6 May 2025 (‘Operation Sindoor’) after the Pahalgam attack of 22 April that killed 26, and a US-brokered ceasefire has held since May 2025. CFR’s tracker, updated 6 November 2026, records an Indian destroyer colliding with a Pakistani patrol vessel in the Arabian Sea on 15 September 2026, the first direct military confrontation since, and Indian border guards shooting Pakistani civilians in the Bedian sector on 2 October.

conflicts.t: China, which claims Taiwan and has not renounced force, massed more than 100 naval and coast guard vessels across the western Pacific in early November 2026 in unannounced drills larger than the ‘Justice Mission 2025’ exercise, with simulated attacks on cities and a submarine-launched intercontinental missile fired from the Yellow Sea. About 70 vessels were still inside the first island chain on 13 November as Beijing prepared to host APEC in Shenzhen; Taipei called it ‘silent intimidation’.

conflicts.t: The 1953 armistice holds. North Korea fired several missiles from Sondok toward the East Sea on 4 November 2026 and said it had tested a new air-defence missile; in September it tested a hypersonic short-range system and commissioned a second Choe Hyon-class destroyer that Kim Jong Un called nuclear-capable. No US–North Korean talks are announced: Pyongyang wants Washington to drop denuclearisation first, while President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea urges sanctions relief for a freeze (Arms Control Today, October 2026).

Pashinyan, Aliyev and Trump signed a declaration in Washington in August 2025; on 18 November 2026 Pashinyan said the 42 km TRIPP corridor across Armenia to Nakhchivan, with road, rail and pipelines, is ‘entering the practical implementation phase’ and that the southern border must now be delimited (Interfax). A UN-mediated ‘4+4’ roadmap signed in Tripoli on 30 August 2026 promises presidential and parliamentary elections within 24 months under a single executive, and the rival militaries have held unification talks and joint drills at Sirte under US supervision.

Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August 2026 on a hard-line platform; Colombia Reports wrote on 11 November that in his first 90 days the Ombudsman and police recorded rises in homicide, extortion and attacks on the security forces, with 38 police and soldiers killed, and on 10 November the ELN hit a military base in Norte de Santander with a drone.

IOM counted 1,235 people fleeing attacks or fear of attacks in Mocímboa da Praia, Macomia, Muidumbe and Meluco between 14 and 27 October 2026, 584 of them children. On 2 November Secretary Rubio set out a three-phase plan of stabilisation, recovery and democratic transition, and on 18 November Pete Hegseth visited Caracas and signed an agreement restoring military ties; no election date is set, and AP counts at least 240 killed in US strikes on alleged drug boats since September 2025.

On 23–24 July 2026 twelve Chinese coast guard and three militia vessels hit two Philippine ships with water cannon at Scarborough and came within 7 metres of a fisheries boat; on 20 July a Filipino sailor was struck with a baton at Second Thomas Shoal, both sides summoned ambassadors, and Marco Rubio reaffirmed the US defence treaty in Manila.

src: Al Jazeera, Philippines accuses China of using water cannon on vessels for second day (24 Jul 2026)

events.n: US midterm elections: Democrats take both chambers
events.t: In the midterm elections of 3 November 2026 the Democrats won control of the House and the Senate, ending the Republican trifecta. By the morning of 4 November they led the House 228–139 with 19 seats gained and had flipped seven Senate seats for a 54–44 majority, with Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled; James Talarico’s defeat of Ken Paxton in Texas was the party’s first statewide win there in more than 30 years. Trump said: ‘I have total veto power, so they have to come to us.’
src: WSB-TV (Cox Media Group), Election 2026: Democrats capture both chambers of Congress (4 Nov 2026)

events.n: North Korea fires missiles into the East Sea
events.t: South Korea’s military detected several missiles fired on the morning of 4 November from the Sondok area, about 170 km north-east of Pyongyang, toward the East Sea; KCNA said the North had tested a new air-defence missile and rehearsed a fire strike. No talks with Washington are announced, and the FBI blames Pyongyang for the theft of more than $6bn in cryptocurrency from Binance (Stars and Stripes, 5 November).
src: Stars and Stripes, North Korea tests air-defence missile as diplomacy stalls (5 Nov 2026)

events.t: Myanmar’s election commission announced on 6 November by-elections on 4 April 2027 in 39 constituencies, about a third of them in areas of Sagaing, Mandalay and Chin where voting was cancelled for security reasons during the phased general election of December 2025 and January 2026 that made coup leader Min Aung Hlaing president. Aung San Suu Kyi remains detained and her party dissolved; ACLED counts more than 100,000 deaths since the 2021 coup.
src: The Star (AFP), Myanmar announces by-elections expanding parliament writ (6 Nov 2026)

events.t: The UN climate conference COP31 runs from 9 to 20 November 2026 at the Antalya Expo Center under a Turkish presidency, with Australia’s Chris Bowen as president of negotiations and a leaders’ summit on 11–12 November. The opening plenary on 9 November adopted a standalone Climate Finance Work Programme demanded by developing countries, over EU objections, and dropped separate agenda items on tripling adaptation finance and on climate-related trade measures; UNEP puts developing countries’ adaptation needs at $305bn a year by 2035.
events.fig: adaptation needs of $305bn a year by 2035 against $28.2–31.7bn of international public adaptation finance in 2024 (UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026)
src: Down To Earth, COP31 adopts climate finance work programme; proposals for adaptation funding, trade measures dropped (10 Nov 2026)

events.n: Ukraine, Russia and the US talk in Abu Dhabi
events.t: Ukraine, Russia and the United States held their first talks since February on 10–11 November 2026 in Abu Dhabi, without Germany, France or Britain. Russia’s delegation head Vladimir Medinsky said he would be satisfied ‘only when we win and sign a peace agreement on our terms’; Russia demands territory and a NATO pull-back from members that joined after 1997, Ukraine wants an Article 5-style guarantee, and the sides agreed to exchange at least 1,000 prisoners each (Al Jazeera, 13 November).
src: Al Jazeera, Russia’s demands come from a different reality as war effort stagnates (13 Nov 2026)

events.t: In early November 2026 China massed more than 100 naval and coast guard vessels across the western Pacific and around Taiwan in unannounced drills larger than ‘Justice Mission 2025’, with all three theatre commands, the Liaoning carrier group east of the Philippines, simulated attacks on cities and a submarine-launched intercontinental missile fired from the Yellow Sea into the Chinese mainland. About 70 vessels remained inside the first island chain on 13 November; Taipei called it ‘silent intimidation’ before the APEC summit.
events.fig: more than 100 vessels at the peak; about 70 inside the first island chain on 13 November
src: Honolulu Star-Advertiser (Reuters), China stages unannounced Pacific drills in intimidation of Taiwan (13 Nov 2026)

events.n: Sudan’s army takes al-Khuwai in West Kordofan
events.t: The Sudanese Armed Forces took al-Khuwai, a main town of West Kordofan, on 13 November 2026, weeks after breaking the RSF siege of El Obeid with allied Darfur forces; the capture opens routes toward Babnusa and North Darfur. The RSF still holds al-Nuhud, parts of South Kordofan and all five Darfur states, and Al Jazeera puts the war’s toll at about 150,000 dead and more than 14 million displaced.
src: Al Jazeera, How SAF successes in Sudan’s Kordofan could turn the tide against the RSF (14 Nov 2026)

events.t: SpaceX’s Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase, Texas, at 5.47 pm EST on 13 November 2026; the Super Heavy booster logged a low-fuel alarm, diverted to the Gulf and was destroyed by its flight-termination system, but Ship 42 deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, flew 14 orbits in nearly a day and at 4.18 pm EST on 14 November was caught by the launch tower’s ‘chopstick’ arms, the first catch of a Ship returning from orbit (Space.com).
events.fig: 26 Starlink V3 satellites deployed; 14 orbits; 33 Raptor 3 engines and more than 18 million lbf of thrust at lift-off
src: Space.com, Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch (Nov 2026)
Nature World News, SpaceX targets Friday 13th for first attempt to catch both Starship stages (11 Nov 2026)

events.t: The ASEAN summit opened in Manila on 15 November 2026 under Philippine chairmanship, with Brazil’s Lula and Canada’s Mark Carney among the guests, tariffs and the Middle East on the agenda and the South China Sea code of conduct said to be 80% negotiated; nearly 20,000 police were deployed and about 200 protesters clashed with police on the first day. Trump arrived on 17 November for the first Quad meeting of his second term with India, Japan and Australia before flying to Shenzhen (The Star, 15 November; RFA, 18 November).
src: The Star, ‘Trump coming’: trade war in focus at ASEAN summit ahead of the US president’s arrival (15 Nov 2026)
Radio Free Asia, Smiles and hugs ahead of Trump, Xi and Putin’s highly anticipated meeting (18 Nov 2026)

events.n: Houthis take the Bab al-Mandeb coast
events.t: On 15 November 2026 Yemen’s Southern Armed Forces announced a ‘repositioning’ away from Dhubab airport and the Bab al-Mandeb area in western Taiz to defend Aden and relieve besieged Taiz; the Houthis claimed to have expelled them and by 16 November had advanced about 50 miles along the Gulf of Aden coast, to within reported reach of Aden. Saudi Arabia replaced its Joint Forces commander the same day as its coalition intercepted Houthi drones over Riyadh and Mecca.
events.fig: OCHA: more than 340,000 displaced since August 2026
src: FDD’s Long War Journal, Houthis retake Bab al-Mandeb and move toward Aden (16 Nov 2026)
Al-Monitor, Yemen’s Saudi-backed forces retreat to defend Aden as Houthis advance (16 Nov 2026)

events.n: New York’s November sales: records for Van Gogh, Kandinsky and Kusama
events.t: Sotheby’s opened the marquee week on 16 November 2026 with $378.7m across two evening sales and a $15m record for Yayoi Kusama, who died in August; Christie’s 20th-century sale on 17 November made $627m with fees, with Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken (1923) at $85.8m, a record, Klimt’s Litzlbergkeller at $82.3m and a Jeff Koons-consigned group at $104.7m. On 18 November Van Gogh’s Blossoming Chestnut Trees (1890), its Nazi-era provenance settled a day earlier, sold at Sotheby’s for $190.4m with fees to William Acquavella, a record for the artist though below its $180m estimate on the hammer.

events.n: Israel’s first ground push in Gaza since the ceasefire
events.t: On 18 November 2026 Israeli tanks advanced east of the Nuseirat camp and north of Bureij in central Gaza in the first broad ground operation since the October 2025 ceasefire; the army said it was removing a threat to its forces at the ‘Yellow Line’, hospital officials reported three Palestinians killed and residents of Maghazi and Bureij fled without an evacuation order. Hamas called it a flagrant violation, and the Board of Peace had warned the truce faced collapse.
src: Al Jazeera, Palestinians flee refugee camp as Israel begins operation in central Gaza (18 Nov 2026)
UN OCHA, Gaza Reported Impact Snapshot (4 Nov 2026)

events.n: The US and Venezuela restore military ties
events.t: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Caracas on 18 November 2026, met acting President Delcy Rodríguez and signed an agreement restoring military ties covering training, intelligence sharing and equipment, calling Venezuela ‘a compliant security partner’ ten months after the 48-minute operation that seized Nicolás Maduro. No election date is set; AP counts at least 240 killed in US strikes on alleged drug boats since September 2025.
src: WFSB (AP), US and Venezuela sign a deal to re-establish military ties, Hegseth says on visit to interim leaders (18 Nov 2026)
Al Jazeera, US urges Venezuela to follow phased plan for democratic transition (3 Nov 2026)

events.n: Armenia says the TRIPP corridor enters implementation
events.t: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on 18 November 2026 that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, a 42 km road, rail and pipeline corridor across southern Armenia linking Azerbaijan to Nakhchivan and on to Turkey, is ‘entering the practical implementation phase’, and that the southern Armenian–Azerbaijani border must now be delimited; he and Ilham Aliyev reaffirmed their agreements at a meeting in Dublin (Interfax).
src: Interfax, Pashinyan: TRIPP project entering practical implementation phase (18 Nov 2026)

events.n: APEC in Shenzhen and the Trump–Xi–Putin summit
events.t: The 33rd APEC leaders’ meeting ran in Shenzhen on 18–19 November 2026; Xi Jinping met Trump at the foot of Air Force One. On 19 November Xi chaired the first three-way summit with Trump and Putin at Kylin Villa, which issued a ‘peace declaration’ pledging talks on nuclear risks and proliferation, stable energy flows and closer cooperation, and criticising the International Criminal Court; it made no mention of Ukraine or Iran, though Trump pressed Xi on the war and said Tehran cannot have a nuclear weapon (Al Jazeera).
src: Al Jazeera, ‘Groundbreaking’ Trump–Xi–Putin summit: five key takeaways (19 Nov 2026)
Radio Free Asia, Smiles and hugs ahead of Trump, Xi and Putin’s highly anticipated meeting (18 Nov 2026)

events.t: On 19 November 2026 Haiti’s armed forces and police, with a task force that included Erik Prince’s Vectus Global, launched an operation to clear gangs from Martissant, the western tip of Port-au-Prince that controls Route 2 to the south and has been in gang hands for more than five years; police said 34 suspected gang members were killed, a figure not independently verified. El Salvador has about 2,500 troops in the country and the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force works in Tabarre, Artibonite and on Route 5 (AP).
src: WCAX (AP), Heavy fighting erupts in Haiti as armed forces fight gangs to regain control of key corridor (19 Nov 2026)

At the glacial maximum, 26,500 to 19,000 years ago, ice covered most of northern Europe and the sea stood 110 to 120 metres lower; people crossed from Beringia into the Americas by about 15,000 years ago. The Löwenmensch ivory figure of 40,000 to 35,000 years ago and Spanish cave art of 40,000 years ago are Europe’s oldest images; the Sulawesi caves are older still.

egypt.sync: Egypt was united about 3150 BC, and the Giza pyramids rose in the Old Kingdom (c. 2686–2181 BC) while Sumerian and Akkadian cities ruled Mesopotamia and traded with the Nile. Drought around 2200 BC brought famine and strife. The Hyksos held the Delta from c. 1785 BC; the New Kingdom, from 1549 BC, reached from Syria to the Fourth Cataract, Akhenaten moved his court to Amarna c. 1350 BC, and Ramesses II sealed the first recorded peace treaty with the Hittites c. 1258 BC. Persia, Alexander and Rome followed.

Alexander died in 323 BC and his generals divided the East, where Koine Greek became the common tongue. Rome won the Punic Wars, took Greece in 146 BC and became an empire under Augustus in 27 BC; the Theodosian decrees of 393 ended the imperial cult.

byzantine.sync: Constantine founded Constantinople in 330, and Justinian (527–65) rebuilt Hagia Sophia after the Nika riots of 532. Arab armies took Syria and Egypt by 642; Leo III removed the Christ icon over his gate in 726, and icons were restored at Nicaea in 787. Papal legates laid a bull of excommunication on Hagia Sophia’s altar in 1054, Manzikert opened Anatolia to the Turks in 1071, the Fourth Crusade sacked the city in 1204 and the Ottomans took it in 1453. Moscow, victor at Kulikovo in 1380, inherited the icon.

The Hundred Years’ War ran from 1337, with firearms at Crécy in 1346; the papacy sat at Avignon from 1309 to 1376 and rival popes split the Church from 1378 to 1417. Florence grew rich on bills of exchange and double-entry bookkeeping, and Dante began the Comedy around 1310.

Movable type spread from a single shop in Mainz around 1440 to some 270 cities, which had printed more than 20 million volumes by 1500. Lorenzo de’ Medici (1449–92) ruled Florence as patron of Botticelli, Leonardo and the young Michelangelo, Matthias Corvinus made Buda a Renaissance court, and Lisbon’s captains worked down the African coast toward India.

The Peasants’ War of 1524–25 ended at Frankenhausen, Zwingli fell in battle in 1531, the protest at Speyer in 1529 gave Protestants their name, and the Peace of Augsburg of 1555 let each prince choose his faith. Luther wrote a fifth of everything printed in Germany in the century’s first third; Antwerp fell to Philip II’s army in 1585.

Francis I routed the Swiss at Marignano in 1515; at Pavia in February 1525 he was beaten and carried captive to Spain. In May 1527 unpaid imperial troops, many of them Lutherans, sacked Rome and besieged Clement VII in Castel Sant’Angelo, while Luther’s theses of 1517 had split the Church in Germany. Cambrai in 1529 sealed Habsburg rule.

The Jesuits were recognised in 1540, the Index of forbidden books first appeared in 1559, and the Inquisition summoned Veronese to explain his Last Supper. Lepanto followed in 1571, the French wars of religion ran from 1562 to the Edict of Nantes in 1598, and Antwerp fell to Philip II’s general Farnese in 1585.

Galileo came to Rome for his trial before the Inquisition in 1633, Charles I was executed in 1649, and Newton published the Principia in 1687. The Manchu took China in 1644, Tokugawa Ieyasu became shōgun in 1603, and the Taj Mahal rose at Agra from 1632. Louis XIV reigned from 1643 to 1715 and enlarged Versailles from 1661.

The Dutch East India Company, formed in 1602 by merging rival traders, razed Jayakarta and built Batavia on it in 1619, and a Dutch fleet broke a Spanish one at the Downs in 1639. Kepler began on the elliptical orbits in 1605 and Galileo was tried in 1633. England fought its civil war from 1642, and Louis XIV invaded the Republic in 1672.

Most of Europe fought the War of the Austrian Succession from 1740 to 1748, and the Seven Years’ War spread across the world from 1756 to 1763. Diderot’s Encyclopédie appeared from 1751, Catherine the Great took the Russian throne in 1762, and James Watt improved Newcomen’s steam engine in 1765. The Qianlong Emperor ruled China from 1735, while the Mughal empire broke apart after Aurangzeb’s death in 1707.

neoclassicism.sync: The American Revolutionary War ran from 1775 to 1783, and the Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence in Philadelphia in 1776. Watt’s improved steam engines were installed from 1776. The Bastille fell on 14 July 1789, and Napoleon won his first battle at Montenotte in 1796 and took power on 18 Brumaire 1799. The partitions of Poland ended the Commonwealth by 1795, Cook mapped the Pacific, and the Napoleonic Wars ran from 1803 to Waterloo.

romanticism.sync: The Napoleonic Wars ran from 1803 until Napoleon’s defeat at Waterloo, and the Congress of Vienna redrew the borders after him. The first steam locomotive ran in 1804 and the Stockton and Darlington, the first public railway, opened in 1825; Niépce made the first photograph in 1827. The July Revolution of 1830 overthrew the Bourbons, Britain fought the First Opium War from 1839, and the revolutions of 1848 shook Europe in the year Marx and Engels published The Communist Manifesto.

realism.sync: Louis-Philippe ruled France from the July Revolution of 1830 until the February barricades of 1848, when Louis-Napoleon was elected president; he made himself Napoleon III in 1852 and set Haussmann to rebuild Paris from 1853. Britain, France and the Ottomans fought Russia in the Crimea in 1853–56. Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, Russia abolished serfdom in 1861 and America fought its Civil War from 1861 to 1865. Napoleon III fell with the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71.

peredvizhniki.sync: Russia abolished serfdom in 1861, and the great novels came out beside the Wanderers’ shows: Dostoevsky’s Crime and Punishment in 1866 and The Brothers Karamazov in 1879–80, Tolstoy’s War and Peace in 1869. Mendeleev presented the periodic table on 6 March 1869. Nicholas II was crowned in Moscow in 1896, Bloody Sunday opened the revolution of 1905, the Bolsheviks took power in 1917, and the capital moved from Petrograd to Moscow in 1918.

prerapha.sync: Victoria had reigned since 1837. The revolutions of 1848 shook Europe, and on 10 April that year the Chartists held a ‘monster’ rally on Kennington Common. The Brotherhood first showed in May 1849, Millais’s Isabella at the Royal Academy, and the Great Exhibition opened in the Crystal Palace on 1 May 1851. Britain fought in the Crimea in 1853–56, Dickens published Bleak House in 1853 and Hard Times in 1854, and Darwin’s On the Origin of Species appeared in 1859.

ukiyoe.sync: Tokugawa Ieyasu became shōgun in 1603 and made Edo the seat of government; it grew from about 1,800 people to more than a million. From 1790 every print needed a censor’s seal, and Utamaro was jailed in 1804 for prints of Hideyoshi; the Tenpō Reforms of 1841–43 banned courtesans and actors, so artists turned to landscape. Perry reached Edo in 1853, the Convention of Kanagawa opened Japan in 1854, and the Meiji Restoration of 1868 and the Boshin War ended the shogunate.

chineseink.sync: The Jin moved their capital to Zhongdu, today’s Beijing, in 1153, and Zhu Xi (1130–1200) made the neo-Confucian synthesis whose commentaries set the civil-service examinations from 1313 to 1905. Kublai Khan began Dadu in 1267 and made it the capital of all China in 1279; Marco Polo lived some 17 years in his lands. The Yongle Emperor moved the Ming capital to Beijing in 1421, the Manchus took the city on 3 May 1644, and the Xinhai Revolution of 1911 ended the empire.

academic.sync: Louis-Napoleon made himself Emperor Napoleon III on 2 December 1852 and set Haussmann to rebuild Paris from 1853; the Palais Garnier was among the new monuments. Baudelaire and his publisher were prosecuted for Les Fleurs du mal in 1857, and in 1863 his Painter of Modern Life defined modernity as ‘the transitory, the fugitive, the contingent’. Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, the Franco-Prussian War ended the Second Empire in 1870, and the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 divided Africa.

The first telephone call was made in 1876, Edison patented a practical light bulb in 1879 and Karl Benz sold the first commercial motor car in 1886. The Berlin Conference of 1884–85 carved up Africa.

Freud published The Interpretation of Dreams in Vienna in 1899, and the Boxer Rebellion was put down by eight nations in 1901. Paris drew millions to its expositions and the Eiffel Tower. Japan defeated Russia in 1904–05, the Russian Revolution of 1905 followed, and Einstein published special relativity the same year.

artsandcrafts.sync: The Great Exhibition opened in the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park on 1 May 1851, and the Museum of Manufactures, forerunner of the Victoria and Albert Museum, opened at Marlborough House in 1852. Edison patented a practical light bulb in 1879, large electric utilities followed from 1882 and Karl Benz sold the first motor car in 1886. The Berlin Conference of 1884–85 divided Africa, the Wiener Werkstätte was founded in Vienna in 1903, and the First World War began in 1914.

viennasecession.sync: The Secession was founded in April 1897, and its building and the Stadtbahn opened in 1898. Freud’s The Interpretation of Dreams was published in Vienna on 4 November 1899, the year the magazine Die Fackel began. The Wiener Werkstätte followed in 1903 and the Vienna Psychoanalytic Society in 1908. The First World War began in 1914, Franz Joseph I was buried on 30 November 1916, and defeat in 1918 opened the years of Red Vienna.

miriskusstva.sync: Nicholas II was crowned in 1896, and the Moscow Art Theatre was founded in 1898. Japan defeated Russia in 1904–05, and Bloody Sunday in January 1905 opened the revolution that brought the St Petersburg Soviet. Akhmatova joined the Acmeists around 1910, published Evening in 1912 and frequented the Stray Dog cabaret. The capital was renamed Petrograd in 1914, and after 1917 between 900,000 and 2 million Russians emigrated; Bakst, Diaghilev, Pavlova and Nijinsky were among the émigrés.

Japan and Russia fought over Manchuria and Korea in 1904–05, and the defeat set off the Russian Revolution of 1905, a wave of mass unrest across the empire. In 1905 Einstein published special relativity and the equation of mass and energy. Louis Vauxcelles named the Fauves at the Salon d’Automne that autumn; by 1907 they no longer shocked anyone, and Picasso was painting Les Demoiselles d’Avignon.

In 1914 the First World War began; it killed up to 17 million people by 1918, and Einstein proposed general relativity in the middle of it, in 1915. The Expressionists worked largely between that war and the next.

cubism.sync: Picasso painted Les Demoiselles d’Avignon in Paris in the summer of 1907, four years after the Wright Flyer’s first flight and two after Einstein’s special relativity. Russia was still shaken by its defeat by Japan and the revolution of 1905. Kandinsky published Concerning the Spiritual in Art in 1911, and Duchamp became famous after the Armory Show in New York in 1913. The First World War broke out in 1914 and killed up to 17 million people by 1918.

futurism.sync: The poet Marinetti founded Futurism in the first decade of flight: the Wright Flyer had flown in 1903. The First World War of 1914–18 killed up to 17 million people; Boccioni died in 1916, in the middle of it. The Bolsheviks took Russia in 1917, influenza killed between 17 and 100 million in 1918–19, and fascism gained ground in Italy, Germany and Spain through the 1920s. The Great Depression began in 1929, Franco rebelled in 1936 and the Second World War began in 1939.

russianavantgarde.sync: Malevich founded Suprematism, an art of ‘the supremacy of pure artistic feeling’, and Rodchenko and Tatlin founded Constructivism. Petrograd took that name in 1914; the February Revolution of 1917 was followed by the October Revolution, and in March 1918 Moscow became the capital. The Comintern held its founding congress there in 1919, the Lenin Mausoleum was built in 1924, the year Petrograd became Leningrad, Kirov was assassinated in 1934 and the Moscow Metro opened on 15 May 1935.

dada.sync: Dada began in neutral Zürich during the First World War, which killed up to 17 million people between 1914 and 1918. The Bolsheviks set up the first communist state in 1917, and the influenza pandemic of 1918–19 killed between 17 and 100 million. Germany became the Weimar Republic; Hitler’s Beer Hall Putsch failed in 1923, and fascism gained ground in Italy, Germany and Spain. By 1923 Duchamp had given up art for chess.

Paris drew artists from around the world between the wars and reached its peak population of 2.1 million in 1921. Germany became the Weimar Republic, Hitler’s Beer Hall Putsch failed in 1923, and the Great Depression began in 1929. Einstein left Nazi Germany for Princeton in 1933, and the Nazis condemned modern art as degenerate and promoted heroic realism.

The Great Depression began in 1929, Einstein left Nazi Germany for Princeton in 1933, and the Nazis condemned modern art as degenerate. Franco rebelled against the Spanish Republic in 1936, the year of the London International Surrealist Exhibition, and Picasso answered the war with Guernica. Freud fled Vienna for London in 1938, and the Second World War began in 1939.

The Chrysler Building went up in 1930 and the Empire State Building in 1931. Fascism gained ground in Italy, Germany and Spain, Einstein left Nazi Germany in 1933, Franco rebelled against the Spanish Republic in 1936, and the Second World War began in 1939.

mexicanmuralism.sync: The Mexican Revolution of 1910–20 reached the capital: Villa and Zapata briefly held it, and Huerta’s coup of February 1913, the Decena Trágica, ousted Madero, who was killed. The Secretariat of Public Education made its headquarters in the city in 1921, the Palacio de Bellas Artes was inaugurated in 1934 and the Taller de Gráfica Popular founded in 1937. Trotsky was assassinated there on 21 August 1940, the university city was built in 1954, and the Tlatelolco massacre came on 2 October 1968.

harlemrenaissance.sync: In the first Great Migration, from 1910 to 1940, about 1.6 million Black Americans left the rural South for the industrial North, drawn by wartime labour shortages and driven by Jim Crow laws and the boll weevil, and Caribbean immigrants also fed the Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s. The Armory Show brought modern art to New York in 1913, the First World War ended in 1918, MoMA opened in 1929 as the Depression began, and Jacob Lawrence’s Migration Series was shown at MoMA in 1941.

abex.sync: The Second World War ended with the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945, the year the United Nations was founded. The Cold War began in 1947, Israel was created in 1948 and the People’s Republic of China in 1949, and Korea was at war from 1950 to 1953. Robert Coates coined ‘abstract expressionism’ in 1946, and the Irascibles boycotted the Metropolitan Museum’s exhibition American Painting Today – 1950.

colorfield.sync: Greenberg grouped Rothko, Newman and Still as Colour Field painters, and Louis and Noland formed the Washington Color School. The Korean War ran from 1950 to 1953 and the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957. In 1959 the Guggenheim’s new building opened in New York and MoMA’s ‘16 Americans’ showed Stella’s stripes. The Cuban Missile Crisis brought the superpowers to the brink, and US Marines landed near Da Nang in March 1965.

gutai.sync: The American raid of 9–10 March 1945 killed more than 100,000 people in Tokyo, and the US occupation under MacArthur lasted until 1952; the Tokyo War Crimes Tribunal opened in 1946. The Korean War ran from 1950 to 1953 and Sputnik flew in 1957. The economic miracle and the 1964 Olympics rebuilt the capital, and the Tōkaidō Shinkansen began service that year. Tokyo passed a pollution-control ordinance in 1969, and Zengakuren students marched over Okinawa in 1971.

cobra.sync: Germany occupied Paris from 1940 to 1944, and the Fourth Republic followed in 1946. Camus published The Stranger in 1942 and The Plague in 1947, Sartre, Beauvoir and Merleau-Ponty founded Les Temps modernes in October 1945, and The Second Sex appeared in 1949. Dubuffet coined ‘art brut’ just after the war. The Cold War began in 1947, the People’s Republic of China was founded in 1949, and The Rebel of 1951 ended Camus’s friendship with Sartre.

pop.sync: Lawrence Alloway first used the term ‘Pop Art’ in 1956, and Warhol opened his first Factory in New York in 1962. The Soviet Union had launched Sputnik in 1957; the Cuban Missile Crisis brought the superpowers to the brink, and US Marines landed near Da Nang in March 1965. The Tet Offensive of January 1968 hurt American support for the war, Czechoslovakia had its Prague Spring that year, and Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969.

minimalism.sync: Stella’s stripe paintings appeared in MoMA’s ‘16 Americans’ in 1959, Judd wrote ‘Specific Objects’ in 1964, and Michael Fried attacked Robert Morris in ‘Art and Objecthood’ in 1967. US strength in Vietnam peaked at about 543,400 troops in April 1969, the year Apollo 11 landed on the Moon. National Guardsmen killed students at Kent State in May 1970, the Paris Peace Accords were signed in January 1973, and after the Yom Kippur War OPEC used an oil embargo.

conceptual.sync: Warhol opened his first Factory in 1962. After the Gulf of Tonkin incident of August 1964 Congress passed its resolution, and US Marines landed near Da Nang in March 1965. The Tet Offensive of January 1968 hurt American support for the war, Czechoslovakia had its Prague Spring, and the Stonewall riot of 1969 helped start the modern gay rights movement in the year of Apollo 11. The Paris Peace Accords followed in 1973, and then OPEC’s oil embargo.

arteprovera.sync: The Tet Offensive of January 1968 hurt American support for the war in Vietnam, and Czechoslovakia had its Prague Spring the same year. US strength in Vietnam peaked at about 543,400 troops in April 1969, and Apollo 11 landed on the Moon that year. National Guardsmen killed students at Kent State in May 1970. The Paris Peace Accords were signed on 27 January 1973, and after the Yom Kippur War OPEC used an oil embargo that opened the energy crisis.

monoha.sync: Tokyo had rebuilt for the 1964 Olympics and the Tōkaidō Shinkansen. The high-rise Kasumigaseki Building was finished in 1968, and the city passed a pollution-control ordinance in 1969. Zengakuren students demonstrated in 1971 against the terms of Okinawa’s return, and the Nakagin Capsule Tower went up in 1972. Abroad the Tet Offensive of 1968, Apollo 11 in 1969, the Paris Peace Accords of January 1973 and OPEC’s oil embargo after the Yom Kippur War framed the years.

dansaekhwa.sync: Seoul changed hands four times in the Korean War of 1950–53 and was largely destroyed, and refugees swelled it to about 2.5 million. It annexed the towns around it in 1963, and the industrialisation of the 1960s and 1970s raised living standards sharply. By 1980 the city held 8,364,379 people, a high-rise building boom followed, and in 1988 Seoul hosted the Olympics and opened the Seoul Museum of Art. Abroad, OPEC’s oil embargo of 1973 and the fall of Saigon in 1975 marked the decade.

photorealism.sync: US forces left Vietnam by March 1973 and Saigon fell on 30 April 1975. After the Yom Kippur War of 1973 OPEC’s oil embargo opened the energy crisis. In New York the twin towers of the World Trade Center were completed on 4 April 1973, the Daily News ran ‘Ford to City: Drop Dead’ on 30 October 1975, Studio 54 opened in April 1977, and a blackout that July was followed by rioting and looting.

neoexpressionism.sync: Martial law was imposed in Poland in 1981, the year the CDC reported the first cases of what became AIDS; New York had the most American cases. Western painting counts Basquiat, Haring and Schnabel among the American neo-expressionists and Richter and Kiefer among the European ones. The Chernobyl reactor exploded in 1986, the Dia Center for the Arts opened in New York in 1987, and in 1989 revolutions freed Eastern and Central Europe while protesters filled Tiananmen Square.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of New York City

pictures.sync: The work came after New York’s fiscal crisis of 1975, when the Daily News ran ‘Ford to City: Drop Dead’, and the blackout of July 1977 with its rioting and looting. The CDC reported the first AIDS cases in June 1981, and New York had the most American cases. Martial law came to Poland in 1981, the Chernobyl reactor exploded in 1986, the Dia Center for the Arts opened in 1987, and the revolutions of 1989 freed Eastern and Central Europe.

yba.sync: The revolutions of 1989 freed Eastern and Central Europe, Germany reunited in 1990 and the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991; the Rwandan genocide followed in 1994, and Japan sank into its Lost Decades. In London Tate Modern opened in the former Bankside Power Station in May 2000, with the London Eye and the swaying Millennium Bridge, and in 2011 it showed Damien Hirst’s For the Love of God. Four suicide bombers killed 56 people on London’s transport on 7 July 2005.

chinesecontemporary.sync: Protesters filled Tiananmen Square in Beijing in 1989, the year revolutions freed Eastern Europe, and the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991. Lehman Brothers went bankrupt on 15 September 2008 and the financial crisis followed. Ai Weiwei filled the Turbine Hall of Tate Modern with Sunflower Seeds from October 2010 to April 2011. COVID-19, identified in Wuhan in December 2019, was declared a pandemic on 11 March 2020, and the WHO estimates 14.9 million excess deaths in 2020–21.

indianmodern.sync: Pakistan became a dominion on 14 August 1947 and India on 15 August. The Radcliffe Line, revealed on 17 August, displaced an estimated 12 to 20 million people, and most scholars accept about a million dead, above all in Punjab and Bengal. New Delhi, the capital Lutyens inaugurated in 1931, became the capital of India in 1947 and hosted the Asian Games in 1951 and 1982. The Cold War ran from 1947 until the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.

africanmodern.sync: Lagos opened an Art Exhibition Centre and museum in 1943 and founded the Nigerian National Museum in 1957, and most colonised African and Asian countries won independence in the second half of the century. The University of Lagos opened in 1962. FESTAC ’77, the Second World African Festival of Arts and Culture, was held in Lagos in 1977, the federal government moved to Abuja in 1991, and El Anatsui filled the Turbine Hall of Tate Modern in 2023–24.

streetart.sync: New York’s fiscal crisis peaked when the Daily News ran ‘Ford to City: Drop Dead’ on 30 October 1975, and the blackout of July 1977 brought rioting and looting that devastated Bushwick. The first AIDS reports came in 1981, the twin towers fell on 11 September 2001, Lehman Brothers failed on 15 September 2008 and Occupy Wall Street began on 17 September 2011. In August 2024 Banksy’s ninth and final animal in a London series appeared on the gates of London Zoo.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of New York City

digital.sync: Turing described his universal machine in 1936, designed the Automatic Computing Engine in 1945–46 and proposed the imitation game, the Turing test. Apollo 11 reached the Moon in 1969 and the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991. Lehman Brothers failed in September 2008. COVID-19 was declared a pandemic on 11 March 2020 and London went into lockdown on 23 March; Russia invaded Ukraine on 24 February 2022, and UNHCR recorded about 7.8 million Ukrainian refugees in Europe that November.
src: Wikipedia, Timeline of New York City

ultracontemporary.sync: COVID-19, identified in Wuhan in December 2019, was declared a pandemic on 11 March 2020; the WHO estimates 14.9 million excess deaths in 2020–21, and the Tokyo Olympics of 2020 were held in 2021. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, and by September 2025 UNHCR counted 5.7 million Ukrainian refugees worldwide, about 90% of them in Europe. Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, and Banksy’s last London animal appeared at the zoo in August 2024.

superflat.sync: Japan sank into the economic stagnation of its Lost Decades in the 1990s. Tokyo’s metropolitan government moved to a new building in Shinjuku in 1991, and the Tokyo subway sarin attack came on 20 March 1995. The Tokyo International Anime Fair began in 2002. The Great East Japan earthquake and tsunami of 11 March 2011 crippled the Fukushima nuclear plant, and the 2020 Olympics, postponed by COVID-19, were held in Tokyo in 2021.
